items.title: An early look at Matas Buzelis with and without Caleb Wilson.
items.author: Drew
items.body_excerpt:
An early look at Matas Buzelis with and without Caleb Wilson.

With Wilson (206 min): 23.6% usage, 61.0% TS, 4.2 turnovers per 100 possessions.

Without Wilson (57 min): 31.0% usage, 48.7% TS, 7.4 turnovers per 100.

Small sample, but worth monitoring.

quote.author: Drew
quote.text:
With Caleb Wilson sidelined, Matas Buzelis figures to have more opportunities to create offense.

For a rebuilding team still trying to determine his ceiling, that's a meaningful opportunity.

Now we'll get a better look at what he can do with greater offensive responsibility.

items.title: Through five games, Matas Buzelis is averaging 10.6 drives, up from 8.6 last season despite fewer minutes.
items.author: Drew
items.body_excerpt:
Through five games, Matas Buzelis is averaging 10.6 drives, up from 8.6 last season despite fewer minutes.

His shooting on drives has fallen from 53.8% to 35.3%, though he's drawing more fouls.

The aggression is encouraging. The finishing needs work.

Through four games, Matas Buzelis is taking more midrange shots and fewer shots at the rim. His three-point attempt rate is nearly unchanged.

Developing a midrange game is encouraging. 

But is it complementing his ability to attack the basket or coming at its expense?

items.title: My concern with Josh Giddey, even before this news, is how his limitations might affect the development of Caleb Wilson and Matas Buzelis.
items.author: Drew
items.body_excerpt:
My concern with Josh Giddey, even before this news, is how his limitations might affect the development of Caleb Wilson and Matas Buzelis.

The Bulls need him to create advantages in the half court.

If he can't do so consistently, how hard does that make their development?
